words.gram: nominative singular (adjective used as a noun)

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А ты случайно не слишком торопишься?
examples.trans: Are you not rushing things a bit too much?

examples.text: Скажи честно, ты сейчас беременна?
examples.trans: Tell me honestly, are you pregnant right now?

examples.text: Ты едешь туда с этим клоуном?
examples.trans: Are you going there with that clown?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Тебе сделать один горячий капучино?
examples.trans: Should I make you one hot cappuccino?

examples.text: Я уже сделал укол, давление упало.
examples.trans: I already gave an injection, the pressure dropped.

examples.text: Мы сделали много.
examples.trans: We've done a lot.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: До свидания, уходите из моей квартиры.
examples.trans: Goodbye, leave my apartment now.

examples.text: Ладно, проходите уже в комнату.
examples.trans: Fine, go on into the room already.

examples.text: Тебе сделать один горячий капучино?
examples.trans: Should I make you one hot cappuccino?

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.text: Тебе сделать один горячий капучино?
examples.trans: Should I make you one hot cappuccino?

examples.trans: We will forgive him and pour him hot tea.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'a cappuccino' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тебе сделать один горячий капучино?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты всё ещё дуешься на меня?
examples.trans: Are you still pouting at me?

examples.text: Ладно, сейчас всё разберу.
examples.trans: Fine, I will take it all apart now.

examples.text: Шеф, мы уже всё сами решили.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Тебе ещё не надоела серая Москва?

examples.text: Ты всё ещё дуешься на меня?
examples.trans: Are you still pouting at me?

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'are pouting / sulking'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и дуться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and are pouting on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют дуться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to are pouting.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Тебе ещё не надоела серая Москва?
examples.trans: Are you not tired of gray Moscow yet?

examples.text: Там мы найдём тебе хорошую работу.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good').

examples.text: Там мы найдём тебе хорошую работу.
examples.trans: There we will find you a good job.

examples.trans: It is a good thing my passport was in another pocket.

examples.text: Мне тут хорошие чаевые дали.

examples.trans: Tips are good today.

examples.text: Нормально, чаевые сегодня хорошие.
examples.trans: Fine, tips are good today.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.text: Теперь остаётся ждать французских внуков.

examples.trans: Some water, please.

meanings.en: to put, to place, to lay down
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ложить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'you'll put, one can put', paired with 'класть'.

examples.trans: You can put them in the stash for the television.

examples.text: Теперь нужен покой и положительные эмоции.
examples.trans: Now she needs rest and positive emotions.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'their', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я вообще ничего сейчас не понимаю.
examples.trans: I do not understand anything at all right now.

examples.text: Я слышал, они так часто делают.
examples.trans: I heard they often do it that way.

examples.text: Простите, я вас совсем не понимаю.
examples.trans: Excuse me, I do not understand you at all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Тебе ещё не надоела серая Москва?
examples.trans: Are you not tired of gray Moscow yet?

examples.trans: I am kissing you for the first time in five years.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'начка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'secret cash stash' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Настя, неси сюда нашу заначку.
examples.trans: Nastya, bring our secret cash stash here.

examples.text: Положишь их в заначку на телевизор.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'television, TV set' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В телевизор детские вещи не положишь.

examples.text: Положишь их в заначку на телевизор.

examples.trans: Well let us try to settle this right now!

examples.trans: Well, have you lost your minds completely here?

examples.text: Костик, ну прости меня, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Kostik, please forgive me.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.text: Прости, пожалуйста, я совсем случайно.
examples.trans: Forgive me, please, it was completely accidental.

examples.text: Костик, ну прости меня, пожалуйста.

examples.text: Простите, я вас совсем не понимаю.

meanings.en: by the way, speaking of which

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'in the evening', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'ставить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to deliver', paired with 'доставлять'.

examples.text: Пишут, доставим за десять минут.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Может, поедешь со мной в Париж?

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must').

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'борка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'assembly' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Добрый день, а я шкаф собрал.

examples.text: Она у нас уже взрослый человек.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (polite/plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'the two of us, together (two)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы вдвоём одного одолеть не смогли!

examples.text: Хорошо, что паспорт лежал в другом кармане.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Там мы найдём тебе хорошую работу.
examples.trans: There we will find you a good job.

examples.text: Там ведь все мои деньги были.
examples.trans: All of my money was in there.

examples.text: Там вашей маме стало очень плохо.
examples.trans: Your mother has been taken very ill over there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Начинайте наконец налаживать ваши отношения.
examples.trans: Start mending your relationship at last.

examples.text: Там вашей маме стало очень плохо.
examples.trans: Your mother has been taken very ill over there.

examples.text: Скажите, это ваш гостиничный номер?
examples.trans: Tell me, is this your hotel room?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'Mama' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мама, нет, я совсем не беременна.
examples.trans: Mom, no, I am not pregnant at all.

examples.text: А как же мы с мамой?
examples.trans: And what about your mother and me?

examples.text: Там вашей маме стало очень плохо.
examples.trans: Your mother has been taken very ill over there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to become', paired with 'становиться'.

examples.text: Прости, пожалуйста, я совсем случайно.
examples.trans: Forgive me, please, it was completely accidental.

examples.text: У нас дома места всем хватит.
examples.trans: There is enough room for everyone at our place.

examples.text: Оставь Катю в покое и уезжай!
examples.trans: Leave Katya alone and go away!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Там вашей маме стало очень плохо.
examples.trans: Your mother has been taken very ill over there.

examples.text: Почему я до сих пор не в курсе?
examples.trans: Why have I not been informed yet?

examples.text: А почему вы тогда в колпаке?
examples.trans: Then why are you wearing a chef's hat?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Там вашей маме стало очень плохо.
examples.trans: Your mother has been taken very ill over there.

examples.text: Этот клоун может написать плохой отзыв.
examples.trans: This clown can write a bad review.

examples.text: Если ты напишешь о нашем ресторане плохо.
examples.trans: If you write badly about our restaurant.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'корая'). Common feminine noun meaning 'ambulance' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я скоро уезжаю жить в Париж.
examples.trans: I am leaving soon to live in Paris.

examples.text: Пойдём скорее отсюда, мой дорогой.
examples.trans: Let us go quickly from here, my dear.

examples.text: Скорая помощь уже сюда приехала.
examples.trans: The ambulance has already arrived here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мощь'). Common feminine noun meaning 'help' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, может, мы сможем помочь?
examples.trans: Victor Petrovich, maybe we can help?

examples.text: Скорая помощь уже сюда приехала.
examples.trans: The ambulance has already arrived here.

examples.text: Спасибо вам большое за помощь!
examples.trans: Thank you very much for the help!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Настя, неси сюда нашу заначку.
examples.trans: Nastya, bring our secret cash stash here.

examples.text: Пойдём скорее отсюда, мой дорогой.
examples.trans: Let us go quickly from here, my dear.

examples.text: Скорая помощь уже сюда приехала.
examples.trans: The ambulance has already arrived here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'came, arrived (she)', paired with 'приезжать'.

examples.text: Скорая помощь уже сюда приехала.
examples.trans: The ambulance has already arrived here.

examples.text: Ты на какой машине приехала?
examples.trans: Which car did you come in?

examples.text: Паша приехал.
examples.trans: Pasha has arrived.
